items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: People like Hoagy Carmichael, he had no voice, but he was a stylist.

ctx.x: Because Jazz wasn't shit. I mean, it was all right. But when Louis started makin' them records, they changed the whole new concept of (?), about scat singing, and they got the popular singers... Before that, you had to have a...if you'd look on a record, you'd see it had to be a soprano or a baritone, and it specified what you were. When Louis come on, after he started singing "Heebie Jeebies" and doing all that shit, everybody was... They'd come up with the word "song stylist." Is that right? People like Hoagy…
So that's the best compliment I could pay him. And I told about how he kept that roll in his pocket, just for people who don't have nothin'. He would ask you...

items.title: Danny Barker Interview (Louis Armstrong memorial broadcast), 1971-07-09
items.q: See, like, whole Carmichael, people will buy his records.

ctx.x: The music is considered singers. Oh, I see. But then you become a stylist. I see what you're saying. See, with Larry coming on, you become an individual stylist. So people say, well, he always sings cute. See, like, whole Carmichael, people will buy his records. He's got a little thing like something about China, a nice little record. Well, you like it. Yeah, he was really reciting to his music, really. He's not a guy, but he's a stylist. I see what you're saying. You've seen Fats Waller come on, doing his humor.…

...you hear Oakland singing.... ...you hear Oakland singing.... ...you hear Oakland singing.... ...you hear Oakland singing.... ...you hear Oakland singing.... If you've never seen a quaint old southern city Just think of noon or noon And if you haven't seen that town, boy It's a pity There's nothing like New Orleans It will remind you of old-fashioned lace A glass of wine will greet your smiling face And if you've ever seen a brown-eyed gal like my boy You down and do I need you Mm-hmm . . . . . . . . . . . . .…
